lay-mountains.summary: Paint two ranges of far mountains across the canvas, under the sunset sky.
lay-mountains.tip: Far violet makes the back range with its row of peaks, and Mountain blue makes the wide front band in front of it, as the after picture shows; the far blue mountains reach the left and right edges of the canvas. Keep the peaks low and gentle, with no warm light on them yet; the sunset comes later. Below the mountains the sunset sky still shows, as in the after picture; the hills cover it later.
paint_notes: Far violet is pale and can let the orange sky show through: paint it twice, letting the first coat dry.

light-ridges.summary: Skim a faint warm peach glow along the tops of the far mountain ridges.
light-ridges.tip: The sun is low at the right, so keep the peach to the peak tops and the edges facing the sun, most of it on the right side of the far blue mountains. It is very faint in the after picture, so less is better: skim along each ridge with the brush's edge and stop.

lay-lake.summary: Lay a thin pale gold strip of lake at the right edge, under the mountains.
lay-lake.tip: The lake is a thin sliver: its top touches the bottom of the far blue mountains and it runs to the right edge of the canvas. Keep its top edge straight and level, since water lies flat, and let its left end taper to a point as the after picture shows.
paint_notes: Cream gold is light over the blue sky: paint it twice, letting the first coat dry.
